current.text: Minnesota traded Naz Reid and Julius Randle and signed Jonathan Kuminga, who is a poor rebounder. The only bigs on the roster are Gobert, Joan Beringer, Lyles, Freeman and Rocco Zikarsky.
Minnesota may start three guards with a poor-rebounding power forward, so the starting group has little size.
With so little big man depth, he should get more minutes and rebounds. Backup Joan Beringer may not be ready, and no backup looks able to cut into his playing time.
His usage could go up slightly with LaMelo Ball throwing him lobs.
He will have to cover on defense for Kuminga and Ball, who are poor defenders.
Gobert is one of four set starters with Ball, Edwards and McDaniels. Coach Finch rarely changes starters unless someone is hurt.
He is eligible for a contract extension.
He could be traded if Minnesota's season goes badly.
Minnesota is expected to compete, with one prediction of 53 wins, so tank rest is unlikely.
Rank him around 75 to 80 in category leagues. ESPN's rank in the mid 50s is too high. He has limited upside but his utility is fine.
He is decent value compared with Donovan Clingan, who goes far earlier.
Experts disagree on his age decline this season. One expects small declines only, with double-digit rebounds, about two blocks and 60%+ FG. Another thinks he may lose blocks, FG% and usage.
With playoffs ending March 28, Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in weeks 19 to 21. The two-game week is the semifinal, the week starting March 15.
Minnesota has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.

durable.text: He gives elite FG% on solid volume, plus big rebounds and blocks.
His blocks have been under 2 per game in three of the last four seasons.
His free throw shooting is horrendous. He shot 52.6% last season, the second-worst FT impact in the league.
His poor FT% barely matters to managers who punt FT%.
He does not shoot from outside and makes no threes. He adds few assists and scores little.
He is an elite defender, a great screener and offensive rebounder, and durable.
He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Gobert's market price is low: Yahoo value 12 USD with a 5 USD average cost, ESPN value 8 USD with a 6 USD average cost, and he went for 10 USD in our league last season. Expert ranks of 75 to 80 suit a bid of about 8 to 12 USD for his FG%, rebounds and blocks, and he fits best in a punt FT% build, where his 52.6% FT shooting costs nothing. Early in the season, check that he plays more minutes with little big man depth behind him and that his blocks hold near 2 at age 34. Plan around the two-game semifinal week (week 20).
